task_instance: Provision a Neon Object Storage bucket via neon.ts (buckets: { images: {} }), run `neon deploy`/`neon config apply` to create it on a branch, pull the injected AWS_* env vars with `neon env pull`, and use the AWS S3 SDK (or files-sdk) to PutObject/GetObject a small test file against the branch's S3-compatible endpoint, verifying round-trip content and a working presigned URL.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a working bucket/upload flow backed by a real Neon project and branch. This requires: (1) a Neon account and an authenticated `neon` CLI session (neon auth/login), and (2) a live Neon project in one of the supported regions (aws-us-east-2, aws-us-east-1, aws-eu-central-1, aws-ap-southeast-1) with Object Storage enabled. There is no local/offline emulator for Neon Object Storage described in the skill -- it is a hosted, account-bound, credentialed cloud service (the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 env vars are only issued by Neon's control plane for a real branch). The `neon` CLI itself is not installed in this runtime, and installing/using it would still require creating or logging into a Neon account, which the safety rules prohibit (no account-bound services, no credentials/tokens). I could write the neon.ts config and the S3 client code, but could not actually provision a bucket or perform a verified PutObject/GetObject round trip without that account.
evidence: Read SKILL.md in full. Confirmed setup requires `neon deploy`/`neon config apply` against a linked Neon project/branch and `neon env pull` to obtain AWS_* credentials from Neon's control plane -- there is no offline mode. Checked runtime: `which neon` returned nothing (CLI not installed); node v22.22.2 and npm 10.9.7 are available, so the SDK code (files-sdk / @aws-sdk/client-s3) could be written and would run, but only against real Neon-issued credentials and endpoint, which do not exist without creating/authenticating a Neon account. No sample project or emulator was created since the blocking step (account/credential acquisition) occurs before any file storage code could be meaningfully exercised.
